name: 06-lan-gateway
description:
A LAN with a gateway: two PCs on a switch reach each other directly, and the internet through **gw**, which NATs them.

| Container | Address on `192.168.20.0/24` (switch **lan**) | Role |
|---|---|---|
| gw | `192.168.20.1`, plus `nat0` to the internet | default gateway, NAT |
| pc1 | `192.168.20.11` | PC |
| pc2 | `192.168.20.12` | PC |

## Try it
1. **Deploy**, then in pc1's **Console**:
   ```
   ping -c 3 pc2
   ping -c 3 1.1.1.1
   traceroute -n 1.1.1.1
   curl -I https://example.com
   ```
2. Click the **gw–lan** cable and **Capture**: ping pc2 from pc1, then `1.1.1.1`. Only one of them shows up on this cable. Why?
3. In pc2's console, remove its default route and test again:
   ```
   ip route del default
   ping -c 3 pc1
   ping -c 3 1.1.1.1
   ```
4. In gw's console, see the NAT rule counting packets: `iptables -t nat -L POSTROUTING -n -v`.

## Questions
- [ ] Which traffic goes through gw, and which doesn't? How does a PC decide?
- [ ] Without a default route, what can pc2 still reach?
- [ ] The PCs use `1.1.1.1` for DNS. Where do their DNS queries go, hop by hop?

nodes.name: gw
nodes.startup:
# Masquerade everything leaving through nat0 (the way to the internet)
nat-on

nodes.name: pc1
nodes.startup:
# gw is the way out of this LAN
ip route replace default via 192.168.20.1
echo nameserver 1.1.1.1 > /etc/resolv.conf

nodes.name: pc2
nodes.startup:
# gw is the way out of this LAN
ip route replace default via 192.168.20.1
echo nameserver 1.1.1.1 > /etc/resolv.conf

images.dockerlab/router:latest:
FROM alpine:latest

# Networking tools for a gateway or router
RUN apk add --no-cache iproute2 iptables tcpdump bind-tools curl iputils

# nat-on: masquerade traffic leaving through the NAT interface (nat0).
# Safe to run more than once; use it in startup commands.
RUN printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' \
      'iptables -t nat -C POSTROUTING -o nat0 -j MASQUERADE 2>/dev/null || iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o nat0 -j MASQUERADE' \
      > /usr/local/bin/nat-on && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/nat-on
images.dockerlab/host:latest:
FROM alpine:latest

# Everyday tools for an end host: full ip, packet capture, DNS lookups, web requests
RUN apk add --no-cache iproute2 tcpdump bind-tools curl iputils
